payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Are both the mug and the headphones visible enough to compare their positions?
node.criteria: Pass if the mug and headphones are identifiable and their relative positions can be judged; fail if the image clearly shows either is absent or the comparison is impossible; unknown if visibility or identification is inconclusive.
node.binding: Use only the image to identify the mug and headphones and assess whether their relative placement is observable. This establishes evidence availability, not fulfillment.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image clearly shows a mug and headphones, and their relative positions are observable: the mug is to the right of the headphones. Both objects are identifiable enough for comparison.

fulfillment: The binding is too permissive: it asks only whether a mug is to the right of the headphones, so it can mark completion based on any visible mug, without checking that the requested mug was moved from its original position. In the supplied images, the source has one blue mug left of the headphones; the edited image shows a blurred blue remnant on the left and a separate white mug on the right, while the headphones are also altered/cropped. This supports some apparent progress but does not establish that the original mug was moved or that the requested edit is complete. Tighten the node’s typed binding/evidence criteria to track the source mug across the before/after snapshots and assess its displacement relative to the same headphones; distinguish partial progress from a completed relationship, and use unknown if identity or comparison cannot be resolved. The two support observations are highly confident but repeat the same conclusion and do not independently establish object continuity; treat that as an evidence/criterion weakness, not a transport or dependency failure (all checks executed successfully).
s2: The binding checks only the edited image’s final spatial relation, so it can pass for a newly introduced mug and miss whether the requested source mug was moved. Make the typed comparison explicitly use both snapshots: identify the source blue mug and the same headphones, then assess whether that mug’s position changed toward and ultimately to the headphones’ right. Here, the edited image shows a blurred blue remnant on the left and a separate white mug on the right; this is evidence of apparent progress, but does not establish continuity or completion. Preserve partial-progress handling rather than treating the right-side mug alone as fulfillment; use unknown when identity or the comparison cannot be resolved. The headphones also appear altered/cropped, so avoid assuming their identity or position is unchanged. The checks executed successfully: this is a binding/evidence and criterion issue, not a transport or dependency failure. Repeated high-confidence observations of the same final relation are not independent evidence of object continuity.
